docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Defaults are sourced from internal/config/defaults.go. Every flag can also be set through an environment variable (see Environment Variables). cronos-api --help lists them all.

Flag Default Description -node-id (empty) Unique node identifier -data-dir ./data Data directory for WAL, dedup, offsets, snapshots -grpc-addr :9000 Public gRPC listen address -http-addr :8080 HTTP health + metrics address -partition-count 1 Number of partitions (use 8-16 for clusters) -replication-factor 1 Replication factor (production target ≥3) -segment-size 512MB WAL segment size before rotation -index-interval 1000 Sparse index interval (events per entry) -fsync-mode batch every_event | batch | periodic — batch is the durable default, periodic is the throughput ceiling -flush-interval 1000 Background flush interval (ms) -backup-interval 1h How often the node backs up its partitions, at wall-clock multiples of the interval, so the nodes of a cluster back up at the same moment. 0 = no scheduled backups -backup-retention 168h How long a backup is kept. 0 = for good -backup-dir (empty) Where backups go; default backups under -data-dir. A backup on the volume of the data it copies does not survive the loss of that volume -retention-max-age-hours 168 Remove WAL segments older than this many hours, once every consumer group has finished them and the change feed has exported them; in a cluster only the leader removes, from the start of the log (0 = disable) -retention-max-size-gb 0 Keep WAL segments within this many GB by removing the oldest, under the same conditions (0 = disable) -compaction-interval 10m How often finished segments are removed from the start of each log -dev false Developer mode: disables production security requirements -tick-ms 10 Timing wheel tick duration in ms -wheel-size 600 Slots per timing wheel level -hot-window-minutes 60 Events beyond this window go to cold store (0 = disable) -hydrator-min-interval 5000 Minimum adaptive hydrator scan interval in ms -hydrator-max-interval 300000 Maximum adaptive hydrator scan interval in ms -max-ready-queue 1000000 Max ready queue depth per partition (admission control) -max-timing-wheel-size 10000000 Max active timers in hot timing wheel (admission control) -max-in-flight 500000 Max in-flight deliveries per partition (admission control) -ack-timeout 30s Default delivery ack timeout -max-retries 5 Maximum delivery retry attempts -retry-backoff 1s Delay before a retry, multiplied by the attempt number -max-credits 1000 Max delivery credits per subscriber -cb-failure-threshold 0.5 Circuit breaker failure rate to trip (0.0–1.0) -cb-min-attempts 10 Min attempts before circuit breaker evaluates -cb-open-duration-ms 30000 Circuit breaker open duration in milliseconds -dedup-ttl 168 Dedup TTL in hours (7 days) -bloom-capacity 100000000 Bloom filter capacity per partition (100M items) -replication-batch 100 Replication batch size -replication-timeout 10s Deadline for one replication Append RPC to a follower -min-insync-replicas 1 Minimum in-sync replicas (incl. leader) required to ack a write; production target ≥2 -snapshot-catchup-threshold 10000 Intended: replication lag (events) above which a follower requests a full snapshot. Currently a dead config key — parsed but never read; snapshot install is unconditional on the join/SyncPartitionFromLeader path and no lag-driven trigger is wired -raft-dir ./raft Raft data directory -raft-join (empty) Parsed but not used; nodes join through -cluster-seeds -cluster false Enable cluster mode -cluster-gossip-addr :7946 Cluster membership (gossip) TCP address; other nodes reach this node by it -cluster-grpc-addr :7947 Cluster internal gRPC listener (InternalGRPCServer, replication + Raft) -advertise-grpc-addr (empty) Address (host:port) clients reach this node's gRPC port at. Partition metadata gives it to clients, so they reach leaders they were not configured with, nodes added later included. Empty: not given -cluster-raft-addr :7948 Cluster Raft listen address -cluster-seeds (empty) Comma-separated membership addresses of the cluster's nodes. Name every node, on every node -cluster-bootstrap false This node creates the cluster, if it has no state and no other node in -cluster-seeds belongs to one. Give it to exactly one node -cluster-expected-nodes 0 Nodes a new cluster starts with; partitions get their first leaders as soon as that many are up (1 for a single-node cluster). 0 = unknown -cluster-formation-wait 5s With the expected nodes unknown or not all up: how long membership must be unchanged before first leaders are assigned; publishes are refused with a retryable error until then. 0 assigns at once -virtual-nodes 2048 Virtual nodes per physical node in hash ring -heartbeat-interval 1s Cluster heartbeat interval -failure-timeout 5s Node failure detection timeout -suspect-timeout 3s Node suspect timeout -use-memberlist false Not supported; the server refuses to start with it -clock-skew-threshold-ms 5000 Max allowed clock skew from leader in ms (0 = disabled) -node-rack (empty) Rack / AZ label for topology-aware placement -node-zone (empty) Zone label for topology-aware placement -node-region (empty) Region label for topology-aware placement -tls-enabled false Enable TLS for the public gRPC listener -tls-ca-file (empty) Path to CA certificate for public gRPC TLS -tls-cert-file (empty) Path to TLS certificate for public gRPC -tls-key-file (empty) Path to TLS private key for public gRPC -tls-client-auth false Require client certificates on public gRPC (mTLS) -http-tls-enabled false Serve the HTTP port (health, metrics, dashboard, admin API) over TLS with the certificate of the client port -replication-tls-enabled false Mutual TLS for all traffic between nodes: replication, membership and Raft. Needs the three files below -replication-tls-ca-file (empty) CA that signed the certificates of the cluster's nodes -replication-tls-cert-file (empty) This node's certificate, valid for the address other nodes reach it by, for server and client use -replication-tls-key-file (empty) Private key of that certificate -auth-enabled false Enable JWT authentication -auth-jwt-secret (empty) HMAC secret for JWT verification -auth-jwt-public-key (empty) Path to Ed25519/RSA public key for JWT verification -auth-policy-file (empty) Path to RBAC policy JSON file -experimental-features false Enable unverified transactions, online splitting and cross-region replication (CRONOS_REGIONS); requires --dev -exactly-once-commits false Experimental commit-ID storage; rejected in production, does not provide end-to-end exactly-once delivery -follower-reads false Allow follower nodes to serve replay reads -load-shedding-threshold 0.0 Load shedding threshold (0.0-1.0, 0 = disabled) -encryption-enabled false Enable AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for WAL segments -encryption-key-file (empty) Path to 32-byte encryption key file -topic-rate-limit 0 Per-subject per-topic rate limit (events/sec, 0 = disabled) -topic-rate-burst 0 Per-subject per-topic rate limit burst (0 = disabled) -max-memory-percent 80 Publishes are refused while the process holds this share of its memory limit or more (0 = never) -memory-limit 0 Memory the process may use, in bytes. 0 = the container's limit, or the machine's memory -memory-check-interval 1000 How long a memory measurement is used, in milliseconds -max-ingest-rate 0 Max events/sec per partition (0 = unlimited) -ingest-burst-size 0 Token bucket burst size for ingest rate limit -tracing-enabled false Enable OpenTelemetry tracing -tracing-exporter none Tracing exporter (none, stdout, otlp) -tracing-otlp-endpoint 127.0.0.1:4317 OTLP gRPC endpoint for trace export -tracing-sample-ratio 0.01 Sampling ratio (0.0-1.0); lower keeps overhead low -tracing-insecure true Disable TLS when exporting via OTLP -pprof-addr (empty) Serve net/http/pprof (CPU, block, mutex profiles) on this address; empty disables. Must be a loopback address outside --dev

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Every flag can be set through CRONOS_ followed by its name in upper case with dashes as underscores: -cluster-seeds is CRONOS_CLUSTER_SEEDS, -replication-tls-ca-file is CRONOS_REPLICATION_TLS_CA_FILE. Two have different names: CRONOS_DEDUP_TTL_HOURS sets -dedup-ttl and CRONOS_MIN_IN_SYNC_REPLICAS sets -min-insync-replicas. A flag given on the command line wins over the variable.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
v0.7.0 is the current release. Every pull request and every push to main runs the following, and main moves only to a commit on which all of it has passed:

  • build, vet, and the test suite under the race detector, and once without cgo, with the release archives built for five systems;
  • a fault campaign and other acceptance tests against three server processes, with a ledger of every acknowledged event;
  • links cut between three containers of the image, and the image scanned for known vulnerabilities;
  • the production Helm chart in a disposable Kubernetes cluster: TLS, JWT auth, encryption at rest, mutual TLS between nodes, a rolling restart;
  • govulncheck and the dashboard's tests.

The acceptance tests also run three times over every night. What each promise rests on, the known limits, and what v0.7.0 was released without are in the release requirements; findings and their status are in the September and October audits.

Experimental and refused in production: transactions, online partition splitting, cross-region replication, and exactly-once commits.

docs.title: CronosDB Architecture
docs.text:
A distributed, timestamp-triggered event database with built-in scheduling, pub/sub messaging, and WAL-based persistence.

Production readiness note: CronosDB has a development and a production run mode. The --dev flag disables the production requirements for local testing. Without --dev the server refuses to start unless it has TLS, authentication with a policy file, encryption at rest, mutual TLS between nodes, --replication-factor>=3, --min-insync-replicas>=2, --fsync-mode batch or every_event, and, in cluster mode, --cluster-seeds. It also refuses --exactly-once-commits, --experimental-features and a --pprof-addr that is not a loopback address (config.ValidateConfig). See Security and Configuration Reference for details.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
CronosDB is a time-aware event store. Events are published with a future schedule_ts and the system triggers delivery precisely at that timestamp. It combines:

  • Append-only WAL for durable, ordered storage
  • Hierarchical Timing Wheel for O(1) timer scheduling
  • Bloom Filter + PebbleDB for deduplication
  • Raft consensus for cluster metadata, including which node leads each partition
  • Consistent hashing to propose where partition replicas live
  • Synchronous partition replication: a publish is acknowledged once it is on --min-insync-replicas replicas
  • gRPC streaming for pub/sub

Publishing to a partition and delivering its events happen on the partition's leader only. Other nodes answer Unavailable for that partition.

    partition --> snapshot[internal/partition/snapshot.go<br/>recovery snapshot.json]

    replication --> mtls[internal/replication/mtls.go]
    cluster --> raft_pkg[hashicorp/raft]
    dedup --> pebble[cockroachdb/pebble]
    dedup --> rust[Rust FFI - cronos_dedup<br/>cgo builds only, such as the Docker image]
    consumer --> pebble
    storage --> mmap[OS mmap]

docs.title: Request Lifecycle
docs.text: Publishing to a partition and delivering its events happen on the partition's leader only. Every other node answers Unavailable for that partition (ensureClusterPartitionWritable and ensureClusterPartitionLed in internal/api/handlers.go).

docs.title: Publish - Single Event
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant gRPC as gRPC Server
    participant PM as Partition Manager
    participant DD as Dedup Manager
    participant WAL as WAL
    participant REPL as Replication Leader
    participant SCH as Scheduler

    Client->>gRPC: Publish(event)
    gRPC->>PM: GetPartitionIDForKey(partition_key or message_id)
    Note over PM: FNV-1a hash mod partition_count

    gRPC->>gRPC: Leader check
    alt Partition has no leader, is led elsewhere, or leadership is moving
        gRPC-->>Client: Unavailable - retry against the leader
    end

    gRPC->>PM: CanAccept(partition)
    Note over PM: Memory guard (--max-memory-percent), ingest rate,<br/>ready queue, timing wheel and in-flight limits
    alt Over a limit
        gRPC-->>Client: ResourceExhausted - retry with backoff
    end

    gRPC->>DD: IsDuplicate(message_id) claims the ID
    Note over DD: Bloom filter first, PebbleDB only when the filter says maybe
    alt Already accepted or in progress
        gRPC-->>Client: error duplicate message_id
    end

    gRPC->>WAL: AppendEvent(event)
    Note over WAL: Assign offset, CRC32, buffered write
    alt Append fails
        gRPC->>DD: RollbackBatch(message_id)
        gRPC-->>Client: error, a retry is not taken for a duplicate
    end

    gRPC->>REPL: Replicate(event) on a replicated partition
    Note over REPL: Returns once min-insync-replicas replicas,<br/>the leader included, hold the event
    alt Not on enough replicas
        REPL-->>gRPC: error
        Note over gRPC: Event stays in the log, held unaccepted.<br/>A client retry finishes it
        gRPC-->>Client: error replication
    end

    gRPC->>SCH: Schedule(event)
    Note over SCH: Timing wheel slot, or cold store when beyond the hot window
    gRPC->>DD: Put(message_id, offset) records the publish as accepted
    gRPC-->>Client: PublishResponse with offset

docs.title: Publish Batch - High Throughput
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant gRPC as gRPC Server
    participant PM as Partition Manager
    participant DD as Dedup Manager
    participant WAL as WAL
    participant REPL as Replication Leader
    participant SCH as Scheduler

    Client->>gRPC: PublishBatch(events x 1000)
    gRPC->>PM: Group events by partition via FNV-1a
    Note over gRPC,PM: Per partition: leader check (Unavailable)<br/>and CanAcceptBatch (ResourceExhausted)

    par Per-Partition parallel goroutines
        gRPC->>DD: IsDuplicateBatch(messageIDs)
        Note over DD: Batch bloom check then batch PebbleDB claim
        DD-->>gRPC: results array

        gRPC->>WAL: AppendBatch(events)
        Note over WAL: Single lock, single buffered write.<br/>On failure the dedup claims are rolled back

        gRPC->>REPL: Replicate(events) on a replicated partition
        Note over REPL: Until min-insync-replicas hold the batch.<br/>On failure the batch is held unaccepted

        gRPC->>SCH: ScheduleBatch(events)
        Note over SCH: Single lock acquisition for all timers
    end

    gRPC-->>Client: PublishBatchResponse

docs.title: Subscribe and Delivery Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Consumer
    participant gRPC as gRPC Server
    participant CG as Consumer Group
    participant DSP as Dispatcher
    participant SCH as Scheduler
    participant WRK as Worker

    Client->>gRPC: Subscribe(group, topic, partition)
    Note over gRPC: Served by the partition leader only
    gRPC->>CG: JoinGroup(group, member)
    gRPC->>DSP: Register subscription
    Note over DSP: Set credits to MaxCredits

    loop Timing Wheel Tick every tick-ms default 10ms
        SCH->>SCH: Tick and check current slot
        SCH-->>WRK: ReadySignal with expired timers
        WRK->>DSP: DispatchBatch(events)
        DSP->>Client: Stream.Send(Delivery)
        Note over DSP: Credits decremented per event
    end

    Client->>gRPC: Ack(delivery_id, success)
    gRPC->>DSP: HandleAck(delivery_id)
    Note over DSP: Credits incremented back
    gRPC->>CG: CommitOffset(group, partition, offset)

    alt Ack timeout after 30s
        DSP->>DSP: Retry after attempt × backoff
    end

    alt Max retries exceeded
        DSP->>DSP: Send to Dead Letter Queue
    end

docs.title: Storage Engine (WAL)
docs.text: The Write-Ahead Log is the durability backbone. Every event is persisted before acknowledgment.

docs.title: Segment File Structure
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph Segment File
        H[Header 64B] --> R1[Record 1]
        R1 --> R2[Record 2]
        R2 --> R3[Record 3]
        R3 --> RN[Record N...]
    end

    subgraph Header Contents
        H1[Magic: CRNOS1]
        H2[Version: 1]
        H3[First Offset]
        H4[Created Timestamp]
        H5[CRC32 Checksum]
    end

    subgraph Record Format v2
        RF1[Length - 4B]
        RF2[CRC32 - 4B]
        RF3[Raft Term - 8B]
        RF4[Offset - 8B]
        RF5[Schedule TS - 8B]
        RF6[MsgID Len + Data]
        RF7[Topic Len + Data]
        RF8[Payload Len + Data]
        RF9[Payload Checksum - 4B]
        RF10[Meta Count + Entries]
    end

docs.title: Record Binary Format
docs.text:
WAL records use format v2. Each record carries an 8-byte Raft term and a 4-byte payload checksum (written immediately after the payload, before the metadata entries) in addition to the existing fields. Upgrading from older builds requires a clean --data-dir.

Field Size Description Length 4 bytes Total record size including this field CRC32 4 bytes IEEE CRC32 of all bytes after the Length field Raft Term 8 bytes Raft term of the leader that authored the record Offset 8 bytes Monotonically increasing event offset Schedule TS 8 bytes Unix millisecond timestamp for trigger MsgID Len 2 bytes Length of message_id string MsgID N bytes Unique message identifier Topic Len 2 bytes Length of topic string Topic N bytes Topic/channel name Payload Len 4 bytes Length of payload Payload N bytes Arbitrary event data Payload Checksum 4 bytes IEEE CRC32 covering the payload only Meta Count 2 bytes Number of metadata key-value pairs Meta Entries Variable key_len(2) + key + val_len(2) + val per entry

Upgrade note: WAL v2 is not backward-compatible with older segment files. Remove or move the old --data-dir before starting a newer binary.

docs.title: WAL Architecture
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph WAL Per Partition
        BW[Active segment writer<br/>memory mapping, or a 4 MiB buffer when encrypted]
        S1[Segment 0 - offsets 0 to 99999]
        S2[Segment 1 - offsets 100000 to 199999]
        S3[Segment 2 ACTIVE - offsets 200000+]
        NS[Next Segment - created at rotation]
    end

    subgraph Sparse Index Per Segment
        I1[offset=0, pos=64]
        I2[offset=1000, pos=52480]
        I3[offset=2000, pos=104896]
    end

    subgraph Flush Modes
        FM1[every_event - fsync per write]
        FM2["batch - group-commit per batch (default)"]
        FM3["periodic - background flush loop (--dev only)"]
    end

    BW --> S3
    S3 -.->|Rotate when full, synchronously| NS
    S1 --> I1
    S2 --> I2
    S3 --> I3

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale Mapped or buffered appends A plaintext active segment is appended to through its memory mapping. An encrypted segment, or one whose file cannot be mapped, is written through a 4 MiB bufio.Writer, made when the segment is first written to (internal/storage/segment.go) Rotation creates the next segment synchronously Under the WAL lock, starting after the last record actually appended (rotateSegment); nothing is created ahead of time fsync batch or every_event in production The leader and every follower sync before they acknowledge, so an acknowledged publish is on disk on min-insync-replicas replicas. periodic is refused without --dev Sparse index every 1000 events Binary search for O(log N) seeks without full index overhead Memory-mapped reads Zero-copy reads on supported platforms CRC32 per record + trailing checksum + Raft term Detects corruption; enables term-aware replication; tail truncation on recovery Prepared records outside lock Serialization happens lock-free; only offset assignment needs mutex sync.Pool for record buffers Reduces GC pressure under high throughput Atomic file writes via utils.AtomicWriteFile Temp file + fsync + rename + parent-dir fsync for tx logs, encryption key files, etc.

docs.title: Retention Enforcement
docs.text:
The retention enforcer runs every hour (--retention-max-age-hours, --retention-max-size-gb). It picks segments by age and size, and asks the partition to remove each one through Partition.PruneWAL, the same boundary compaction uses (internal/partition/retention.go).

flowchart LR
    A[Hourly retention scan] --> B[Pick segments by age or total size]
    B --> C{Replicated partition and this node is not the leader?}
    C -->|Yes| Z[Skip: follow the leader's log start]
    C -->|No| D{Active segment?}
    D -->|Yes| K[Keep]
    D -->|No| E{Every event due, finished by every group that takes it, accepted, exported by the change feed?}
    E -->|No| K
    E -->|Yes| F[Delete segment and its .index file]
    F --> G[Raise consumer floors to the new log start]

Rules: - Removal goes through PruneWAL, which removes a segment only when every event in it is due, is finished by every consumer group that takes it, is accepted (on a replicated partition, on min-insync-replicas replicas) and has been exported by the change feed. - The active segment is never removed. - On a replicated partition only the leader prunes, and only from the start of the log, so the log stays one unbroken range of offsets. Followers skip the scan; every append names the leader's log start, and a follower removes what lies below it (FollowLogStart). - Unloaded partitions and files outside a partition's segments/ directory are not touched.

docs.title: Compaction Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Compaction timer - every --compaction-interval] --> B{Replicated partition?}
    B -->|Yes, not the leader| Z[Skip: follow the leader's log start]
    B -->|Yes, leader| P[Oldest closed segment first, stop at the first that stays]
    B -->|No| Q[Every closed segment]
    P --> C{Every event due, taken by a group, finished by every group that takes it, exported by the change feed?}
    Q --> C
    C -->|No| K[Keep]
    C -->|Yes| E[Delete segment and index]
    E --> F[Raise consumer floors to the new log start]
    F --> G[Leader: next append tells followers where the log starts]

docs.title: Scheduler and Timing Wheel
docs.text: The scheduler uses a hierarchical timing wheel for O(1) timer management of millions of events.

docs.title: Timing Wheel Structure
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph Level 0 - Root Wheel
        direction LR
        TICK[Current Tick Pointer]
        S0[Slot 0 - Timer List]
        S1[Slot 1 - Timer List]
        S2[Slot 2 - empty]
        S3[Slot 3 - Timer List]
        S59[Slot 59 - Timer List]
    end

    subgraph Level 1 - Overflow Wheel
        O0[Slot 0]
        O1[Slot 1 - Timer List]
        O59[Slot 59]
    end

    subgraph Level 2 - Overflow Wheel
        L0[Slot 0]
        L1[Slot 1 - Timer List]
    end

    TICK -.-> S0
    S59 -->|Full rotation cascades| O0
    O59 -->|Full rotation cascades| L0

Wheel Parameters: - Level 0 (default): 10ms tick, 600 slots = 6 second window - Level 1: 6s tick, 600 slots = 3600 second (60 min) window - Level 2: 3600s tick, 600 slots = 25 day window - Max levels: 10 (hardcoded; only --tick-ms and --wheel-size are configurable)

docs.title: Timer Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pool : sync.Pool.Get
    Pool --> Scheduled : AddTimer
    Scheduled --> InWheel : delay fits in current wheel
    Scheduled --> InOverflow : delay exceeds wheel window
    InWheel --> Expired : Tick advances to slot
    InOverflow --> Cascaded : Overflow wheel rotation
    Cascaded --> InWheel : Recalculate slot in root wheel
    Expired --> ReadyQueue : Push to ready queue
    ReadyQueue --> Dispatched : Worker picks up batch
    Dispatched --> Pool : PutTimer recycle
    InWheel --> Cancelled : RemoveTimer
    Cancelled --> Pool : PutTimer recycle

docs.title: Absolute Time Tracking
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Event arrives with schedule_ts as absolute ms] --> B[now = time.Now in UnixMilli]
    B --> C[delayMs = schedule_ts minus now]
    C --> D[delayTicks = delayMs / tickMs]
    D --> E{delayTicks less than wheelSize?}
    E -->|Yes| F[slot = currentTick + delayTicks mod wheelSize]
    F --> G[Insert into root wheel]
    E -->|No| H[Create or use overflow wheel]
    H --> I[overflowTickMs = tickMs times wheelSize]
    I --> J[Recursively add to overflow]
    J --> K[On cascade: recalculate from absolute ExpirationMs]
    K --> L[No drift accumulation]

docs.title: Cascade Operation
docs.text:
When the root wheel completes a full rotation, timers cascade from the overflow wheel:

flowchart LR
    A[Root wheel completes rotation] --> B[Lock overflow wheel]
    B --> C[Get timers in overflow current slot]
    C --> D[For each timer: recalculate target slot from ExpirationMs]
    D --> E[Bucket timers by target slot using pre-allocated cascadeBuf]
    E --> F[Batch-insert into root wheel slots]

docs.title: Scheduler Recovery on Crash
docs.text:
On restart the scheduler:

  1. Restores wheel origin from timer_state.json when present.
  2. Rebases currentTick from wall clock so absolute fire times stay aligned after downtime (no compounding future skew).
  3. Walks the whole log from its first offset (Wal.GetFirstOffset()), in reads of at most 10,000 events and 16 MiB (replayWALTimers in internal/partition/manager.go).
  4. Events with schedule_ts > now re-enter the hot timing wheel (or cold store).
  5. Events that are already due are not queued. They stay in the log, and a subscription reads what its group has not finished from the log when it starts, at the pace its consumers take it (redriveRetained in internal/api/handlers.go). Nothing is delivered without a subscription, and a backlog larger than memory does not have to fit in memory.

timer_replay_checkpoint.json is still written after the walk, but nothing reads it at start (readTimerCheckpoint and replayWALTimersFromOffset have no callers).

flowchart TD
    A[Node Starts] --> B[Restore timer_state.json if present]
    B --> C[Rebase currentTick from wall clock]
    C --> D[startOffset = first offset of the log]
    D --> G[Read the log, at most 10000 events and 16 MiB per read]
    G --> H{event.schedule_ts > now?}
    H -->|Yes| I[Re-schedule in timing wheel or cold store]
    H -->|No| J[Leave in the log for subscriptions to read]

docs.title: Two-Tier Cold/Hot Scheduler
docs.text:
To keep memory bounded while supporting millions of scheduled events, the scheduler uses a two-tier architecture:

  • Hot Tier: Hierarchical timing wheel (in-memory) for events within the hot window (default 60 minutes).
  • Cold Tier: PebbleDB-backed ColdStore for far-future events (> hot window). Stores only offsets (~16 bytes per event) — full event data remains in the WAL.
flowchart TD
    A[Publish event] --> B{schedule_ts <= now + hotWindow?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Add to Timing Wheel]
    B -->|No| D[Store offset in Cold Store]
    D --> E["PebbleDB key: [schedule_ts:be64][offset:be64]"]

    F[Hydrator Loop adaptive interval] --> G[Scan Cold Store range]
    G --> H[now+hotWindow to now+hotWindow+adaptiveLookahead]
    H --> I[Read full event from WAL via EventReader]
    I --> C

Key Design Decisions:

Decision Rationale Offsets only in cold store WAL is single source of truth; avoids double-writing event data Big-endian composite key [ts][offset] Enables efficient range scans by timestamp Adaptive hydrator interval (5s–5min) Scans more frequently under load, backs off when idle; saves I/O Adaptive lookahead window Lookahead equals current hydrator interval; naturally scans further ahead when running less frequently EventReader interface decouples scheduler from WAL Clean dependency boundary; allows alternative storage backends HotWindowMinutes = 0 disables cold store Full backward compatibility with legacy behavior

docs.title: Deduplication Engine
docs.text: A two-tier deduplication system ensures idempotent publishes with minimal latency.

docs.title: Two-Tier Architecture
docs.text:
graph TB
    REQ[IsDuplicate - message_id] --> BF[Tier 1: Bloom Filter - Go or Rust]

    BF -->|NO - definitely new 99 percent| FAST[Fast Path: Store in PebbleDB + Add to Bloom]
    BF -->|MAYBE - might exist 1 percent| PDB[Tier 2: PebbleDB Lookup]

    PDB -->|Found| DUP[Duplicate - return stored offset]
    PDB -->|Not found - false positive| NEW[New: Store in PebbleDB + Add to Bloom]

Tier 1 - Bloom Filter (In-Memory): - Two implementations behind one interface (internal/dedup/bloom_store.go). NewBloomFilter uses the Rust filter when the binary is built with cgo and the library is linked, and GoBloomFilter otherwise. - Release binaries are built without cgo (CGO_ENABLED=0), where the Rust filter is a stub that returns nil (internal/dedup/rust_bloom_nocgo.go), so they use GoBloomFilter. The Docker image is built with cgo and links the Rust library. - GoBloomFilter: FNV-1a double hashing over uint64 words set with atomic compare-and-swap. - Rust filter: XxHash64 double hashing, AtomicU64 bit arrays, Rayon parallel batch check for 100+ keys. - About 10 bits per ID at a 1% false positive rate: ~120 MB for the default capacity of 100M IDs, allocated on first use

Tier 2 - PebbleDB (Persistent): - 64MB memtable (vs 4MB default) - Internal WAL disabled (our WAL provides durability) - NoSync writes for performance - 7-day TTL automatic expiration

docs.title: Bloom Filter Implementation - Rust FFI (cgo builds only)
docs.text:
This path is used only by builds with cgo, such as the Docker image. No benchmark of it is kept in the repository, so no per-call latency is stated here.

graph LR
    subgraph Go Layer
        GO[rust_bloom_unix.go / rust_bloom_windows_cgo.go - CGO bindings - unsafe.StringData zero-copy]
    end

    subgraph Rust Layer
        RS[lib.rs - AtomicU64 bit array - XxHash64 two seeds - fetch_or lock-free - Rayon parallel batch]
    end

    GO -->|FFI call| RS
    RS --> P1[Add]
    RS --> P2[MayContain]
    RS --> P3[MayContainBatch - parallel for 100+ keys]

docs.title: Batch Dedup Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[PublishBatch: 1000 events] --> B[Phase 1: Batch bloom check via MayContainBatch]
    B --> C[Split into buckets]
    C --> D[Definitely New - bloom NO - ~990 events]
    C --> E[Maybe Exists - bloom YES - ~10 events]

    D --> F[Phase 3: Batch PebbleDB write - single Commit]
    D --> G[Batch bloom.Add for all new keys]

    E --> H[Phase 2: Per-item PebbleDB check]
    H --> I[Actually duplicate: skip]
    H --> J[False positive: store + add to bloom]

docs.title: Bloom Filter Health and Reset
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Hourly PruneExpired] --> B[Delete expired PebbleDB entries]
    B --> C[Check FPR: falsePositives / totalLookups]
    C --> D{FPR > 5 percent?}
    D -->|No| E[Healthy - no action]
    D -->|Yes| F[Set resetInProgress = true]
    F --> G[bloom.Reset]
    G --> H[Clear stats counters]
    H --> I[Set resetInProgress = false]

docs.title: Delivery Pipeline
docs.text: The delivery pipeline moves events from the scheduler to consumers with backpressure control.

docs.title: Pipeline Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    TW[Timing Wheel] -->|ReadySignal| RQ[Ready Queue]
    RQ -->|GetReadyEvents| W[Delivery Worker]
    W -->|DispatchBatch| DSP[Dispatcher]

    DSP --> SH0[Shard 0]
    DSP --> SH1[Shard 1]
    DSP --> SHN[Shard 31]

    SH0 --> SUB1[Consumer A]
    SH1 --> SUB2[Consumer B]

    DSP -->|Timeout or Nack| RH[Retry Heap]
    RH -->|Due| RT[Retry with Backoff]
    RT -->|Max retries| DLQ[Dead Letter Queue - Segments]

docs.title: Credit-Based Flow Control
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Server Dispatcher
    participant C as Consumer Client

    Note over S,C: Initial Credits = MaxCredits 1000

    S->>C: Delivery event_1 - Credits now 999
    S->>C: Delivery event_2 - Credits now 998
    S->>C: Delivery event_3 - Credits now 997

    C->>S: Ack event_1 success - Credits now 998
    C->>S: Ack event_2 success - Credits now 999

    Note over S: Credits > 0 so continue sending
    S->>C: Delivery event_4 - Credits now 998

    Note over S,C: If Credits = 0 then STOP sending and wait for Acks

docs.title: Non-Blocking Retry Heap
docs.text:
The timeoutLoop no longer blocks on inline time.Sleep during retries. Instead, expired deliveries are pushed to a min-heap ordered by retryAt:

flowchart TD
    A[scanExpiredDeliveries] --> B{Delivery timed out?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Push to RetryHeap with retryAt = now + backoff]
    B -->|No| D[Continue]

    E[processRetries on retry loop] --> F{Peek retryAt <= now?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Pop and redispatch]
    F -->|No| H[No-op]
    G --> E

Benefits: - timeoutLoop stays responsive even under retry storms - No goroutine proliferation per retry - Backoff is deterministic and memory-efficient

docs.title: Circuit Breaker
docs.text:
Each subscription has an independent circuit breaker with atomic state machine:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed
    Closed --> Open : FailureRate > Threshold && Attempts >= MinAttempts
    Open --> HalfOpen : OpenDuration elapsed
    HalfOpen --> Closed : Trial success
    HalfOpen --> Open : Trial failure
  • Closed: Normal operation; failures counted
  • Open: Skips dispatch to dead subscriber; fast-fail
  • HalfOpen: Allows one trial after cooldown; re-closes on success

Configuration: - CircuitBreakerFailureThreshold (default 0.5): failure rate to trip - CircuitBreakerMinAttempts (default 10): minimum attempts before evaluation - CircuitBreakerOpenDurationMs (default 30000): cooldown before half-open

docs.title: Delivery Retry and DLQ Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Event dispatched to consumer] --> CB{Circuit Breaker Open?}
    CB -->|Yes| Z[Skip dispatch]
    CB -->|No| B{Ack received within 30s?}
    B -->|Yes success| C[Commit offset, release credits, CB.RecordSuccess]
    B -->|Yes failure| D{Attempt < MaxRetries?}
    B -->|Timeout| D

    D -->|Yes| E[Push to RetryHeap: retryAt = now + backoff]
    E --> F[processRetries pops due entry and redispatches]
    F --> B

    D -->|No| G[Send to Dead Letter Queue]
    G --> H[DLQ Segment: binary record + CRC32]
    H --> I[Available for manual replay or inspection]

docs.title: Dispatcher Sharding
docs.text:
The dispatcher uses 32 shards to reduce lock contention under high concurrency:

graph TB
    subgraph Dispatcher
        HASH[hash of subscription_id mod 32]
        subgraph Shard 0
            S0S[Subscriptions map]
            S0D[Active Deliveries map]
        end
        subgraph Shard 1
            S1S[Subscriptions map]
            S1D[Active Deliveries map]
        end
        subgraph Shard 31
            SNS[Subscriptions map]
            SND[Active Deliveries map]
        end
    end

    subgraph Global Lock-Free
        PI[partitionSubs map - partition to subscribers]
        IFC[inFlightCount - atomic Int64 cap 100K]
    end

    HASH --> S0S
    HASH --> S1S
    HASH --> SNS

docs.title: DLQ Segment Storage
docs.text:
The Dead Letter Queue uses append-only binary segments instead of JSON files:

Feature Implementation Header 64-byte header with "CRNDLQ1" magic Records Binary format identical to WAL (length + CRC32 + payload) Writes Each entry is written to the file and synced when it is recorded; there is no write buffer Rotation 64MB per segment file Recovery On startup, scan dlq/ directory and replay all .dlq segments

Benefits over JSON: - Smaller on disk: no base64 or JSON overhead (not measured here) - Faster append (no marshal/unmarshal) - CRC32 integrity per record - Easy to segment and archive

docs.title: Consumer Groups
docs.text: Kafka-style consumer groups with persistent offset tracking, per-event completion records and group metadata. Delivery is at least once. The leader of a partition sends its groups' progress to its followers (ReplicationService.SyncConsumerProgress), so a follower that takes over does not deliver finished work again, apart from what finished since the last maintenance tick.

docs.title: Consumer Group Model
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph Consumer Group: order-processors
        M1[Member A - Partition 0 and 1]
        M2[Member B - Partition 2 and 3]
        M3[Member C - Partition 4 and 5]
    end

    subgraph Offset Store via PebbleDB
        O1[order-processors:P0 = offset 45230]
        O2[order-processors:P1 = offset 12891]
        O3[order-processors:P2 = offset 78432]
        O4[order-processors:meta = group metadata + assignments]
        O5[order-processors:txn:ID = commit ID, not written by the Ack path]
    end

    subgraph Offset Commit Pipeline
        PEN[Pending Map - in-memory buffer]
        FL[Flush Loop - every 200ms]
        DB[PebbleDB Batch Write]
    end

    M1 -->|CommitOffset| PEN
    M2 -->|CommitOffset| PEN
    M3 -->|CommitOffset| PEN
    PEN -->|dirty flag| FL
    FL -->|batch.Commit NoSync| DB

Persisted state in OffsetStore: - Offsets: per-group, per-partition committed offsets. - Group metadata and assignments: rebalanced partition assignments and member metadata survive restarts. - Commit IDs: OffsetStore.CommitOffsetExactlyOnce can record a commit ID with an offset, but the Ack path does not call it, with or without --exactly-once-commits. Delivery is at least once. Production mode refuses that flag; it needs --dev.

docs.title: Rebalancing
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant M1 as Member A
    participant M2 as Member B - new
    participant GM as Group Manager

    M2->>GM: JoinGroup processors member-B
    GM->>GM: Add member to group
    GM->>GM: rebalanceGroup
    Note over GM: Round-robin partitions across active members
    GM-->>M1: Assigned Partition 0, 2, 4
    GM-->>M2: Assigned Partition 1, 3, 5
    Note over M1,M2: Each member subscribes to assigned partitions

docs.title: Change Data Capture
docs.text:
CDC hands every accepted event to external sinks. It reads a per-partition change feed from the log; nothing runs on the append path.

graph LR
    WAL[Partition log] -->|behind the accepted watermark| Feed[Change feed<br/>one per partition, leader only]
    Feed -->|batches in log order| CDC[cdc.Manager.Deliver]
    CDC --> S1[Kafka sink]
    CDC --> S2[Webhook sink]
    Feed -->|same events| XR[Cross-region replicator<br/>only with --dev --experimental-features]
    Feed -.->|position, at most once a second| Pos[changefeed.json<br/>+ sent to followers]

Behavior: - An event is handed over only once its publish is accepted: not while the publish is in flight, not while it is held after failing past the append, and, on a replicated partition, not before it is on min-insync-replicas replicas. - Events leave in log order, from the partition's leader only. - A sink that fails is offered the same events again (100 ms to 5 s apart). Nothing is dropped and nothing queues in memory; the feed lags instead, and publishing never waits for it. - The feed's position survives restarts and is handed to followers, so a new leader continues it. Delivery to sinks is at least once. - Cross-region replication (CRONOS_REGIONS) is experimental. The server refuses to start with it unless it runs with --dev --experimental-features.

Details and limits: docs/architecture/features/cdc.md.

Leadership is per partition: every node leads some partitions and follows others. The Raft leader of the metadata cluster is a separate role; it commits partition assignments but does not serve a partition's traffic unless it also leads that partition. The partition numbers above are an example.

docs.title: Membership
docs.text:
Every node sends a heartbeat to every other node it knows over TCP (internal/cluster/membership.go). A node that is not heard from is suspected and then counted as dead; it keeps being sent heartbeats, less often, and is taken back as soon as it answers or announces itself. Membership decides who is alive. It does not decide who leads: that is committed through Raft.

A dead node stays a member, and a Raft voter, until an operator removes it with cronos-admin cluster remove-node <node-id>. Remove a node only when it will not come back and is not running.

Traffic between nodes. Nodes talk to each other on three ports: replication (gRPC), membership and Raft. With --replication-tls-enabled all three speak mutual TLS with one set of certificates (internal/cluster/transport.go, internal/replication/mtls.go). A caller must present a certificate signed by the CA in --replication-tls-ca-file before anything it sends is read, and a node checks that the certificate of the node it calls is valid for the address it called. Production mode requires this. Without it the membership and Raft ports are plain TCP, and whoever can reach them can join the cluster as a node and vote.

internal/cluster/memberlist_adapter.go implements the same interface on HashiCorp Memberlist (SWIM over UDP). The server does not use it, and refuses to start with --use-memberlist.

docs.title: Consistent Hashing Ring
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph Hash Ring - SHA-256 with 2048 vnodes per node
        RING[Ring space: 0 to 2 pow 64]
        VN1[Node1 - 2048 virtual positions]
        VN2[Node2 - 2048 virtual positions]
        VN3[Node3 - 2048 virtual positions]
    end

    subgraph Proposed placement - committed through Raft
        PA[partition-0 maps to Node1]
        PB[partition-1 maps to Node3]
        PC[partition-2 maps to Node2]
        PD[partition-7 maps to Node1]
    end

    subgraph Topic Routing
        TR[topic orders via FNV-1a maps to partition 5]
        TR2[topic payments via FNV-1a maps to partition 11]
    end

    RING --> PA
    RING --> PB
    RING --> PC

The ring only proposes where replicas live and which replica would ideally lead. Leadership comes from the assignment committed through Raft (internal/cluster/leadership.go). syncClusterState, on the Raft leader, commits the ring's replica placement, and moves leadership in one of two ways: a fenced election when the committed leader is dead, or a staged handoff when the ring prefers another live replica.

docs.title: Failure Detection and Recovery
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Alive : Node joins
    Alive --> Alive : Heartbeat received
    Alive --> Suspect : No heartbeat for 5 heartbeat intervals (5s)
    Suspect --> Alive : Heartbeat received
    Suspect --> Dead : No heartbeat for 10 heartbeat intervals (10s)
    Dead --> Alive : Answers a probe or announces itself
    Dead --> [*] : cronos-admin cluster remove-node

The timeouts are multiples of --heartbeat-interval (default 1s). A dead node is still probed every fifth heartbeat round. It is removed from Raft and from every node's member list only by cronos-admin cluster remove-node.

Raft leader actions when a partition's leader is dead (checkPartitionHealth and electNewLeader in internal/cluster/leadership.go):

flowchart LR
    A[checkPartitionHealth: committed leader not alive] --> B[Commit: partition has no leader, epoch + 1]
    B --> C[fencedPositions: each reachable replica stops accepting older epochs and reports its log end]
    C --> D{Enough replicas answered to rule out losing acknowledged writes?}
    D -->|No| E[Wait for the next round]
    D -->|Yes| F[Commit the most complete reachable replica as leader, higher epoch]
    F --> G[Nodes follow the committed assignment: promote or step down]

docs.title: Clock Skew Detection
docs.text:
Cross-node heartbeats include timestamps for clock skew monitoring:

flowchart TD
    A[Local heartbeat tick] --> B[Send heartbeat with local timestamp]
    B --> C[Remote node receives]
    C --> D[Compute skew as remote_ts minus local_ts]
    D --> E{Absolute skew over 5 seconds}
    E -->|Yes| F[Log a warning]
    E -->|No| G[Nothing]
  • Compares the remote node's timestamp against local time on every heartbeat (internal/cluster/membership.go).
  • Logs a warning if the absolute skew exceeds 5 seconds. The threshold is fixed in code: the --clock-skew-threshold-ms flag is parsed but nothing reads it.
  • The gauge cronos_clock_skew_ms (no labels) is registered, but nothing sets it, so it stays at 0. Use the log warning, or monitor NTP directly.

docs.title: Replication Protocol
docs.text: CronosDB uses a hybrid replication model: HashiCorp Raft for cluster metadata (partition ownership, leader election, peer set), and a dedicated internal gRPC channel for partition data. Public client traffic never reaches the replication listener.

docs.title: Replication channel layout
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph "Public API listener"
      PUB[gRPC :9000<br/>EventService, PartitionService,<br/>ConsumerGroupService, AdminService<br/>TransactionService: experimental only]
    end
    subgraph "Internal cluster listener"
      INT[InternalGRPCServer :7947<br/>ReplicationService, RaftService<br/>CrossRegionService: experimental only]
    end
    subgraph "HTTP operator plane"
      HTTP[HTTP :8080<br/>health metrics /ui /api/admin]
    end
    subgraph "Public client traffic"
      C[Client SDK] --> PUB
      O[Ops UI / CLI] --> HTTP
      O --> PUB
    end
    subgraph "Intra-cluster traffic"
      L[Leader partition] -->|Append / SyncConsumerProgress| INT
      F[Follower partition] -->|Snapshot, mTLS required in production| INT
      E[Election and topology] -->|Position / LeaderReport| INT
      R[Remote region] -->|CrossRegionService, experimental| INT
    end

The internal listener is InternalGRPCServer (internal/api/internal_grpc_server.go, default :7947, configurable via --cluster-grpc-addr). It registers ReplicationService, and RaftService when cluster mode is on. CrossRegionService is registered there only with --experimental-features, which production mode refuses without --dev (cmd/api/main.go). The same flag gates TransactionService on the public listener (internal/api/grpc_server.go). No public client EventService surface is exposed on the internal socket; cross-region traffic is peer-plane only so arbitrary event inject/fetch stays off :9000.

docs.title: ReplicationService RPCs
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph ReplicationService
      A[Append - unary]
      SN[Snapshot - server streaming]
      PO[Position - unary]
      LR[LeaderReport - unary]
      SP[SyncConsumerProgress - unary]
      S[Sync - server streaming]
    end
    subgraph Use
      A -->|every batch and catch-up| U1[per-batch CRC32, term-fenced, log start]
      SN -->|bulk install| U3[per-file CRC32, atomic dir swap]
      PO -->|elections and handoffs| U4[fenced log position]
      LR -->|topology| U5[ISR and offsets per led partition]
      SP -->|maintenance tick| U6[consumer group progress and change feed position]
      S -->|no caller| U2[served, never called]
    end

The six RPCs are defined in proto/events.proto and served by internal/api/replication_server.go.

RPC Direction Body Used by Append leader → follower (unary) ReplicationAppendRequest{PartitionId, Events, ExpectedNextOffset, Term, PrevLogTerm, Checksum, LeaderId, HasPrevLog, PrevLogOffset, LogStartOffset, LeaderLogEnd} → ReplicationAppendResponse{Success, Error, LastOffset, NextOffset, Term, LogMismatch, ConflictTerm, ConflictFirstOffset} Leader.appendToFollower, from sendToFollower on every replicated batch and from catchUpFollower; also with no events, to announce the log start (announceLogStart) Snapshot follower → leader (server streaming) ReplicationSnapshotRequest{PartitionId, StartOffset, MaxBytes} → stream of ReplicationSnapshotChunk{Header, Data, Trailer} with per-file IEEE CRC32 Follower.InstallSnapshot, from SyncPartitionFromLeader on join, ownership moves and handoffs Position any node → replica (unary) ReplicationPositionRequest{PartitionId, FenceEpoch} → the replica's last offset, last term and epoch Elections (fencedPositions, which fences first) and handoff checks LeaderReport any node → node (unary) → in-sync replicas and offsets of every partition the node leads The admin topology, which shows each partition's ISR as its leader has it SyncConsumerProgress leader → follower (unary) ReplicationProgressRequest{PartitionId, Term, LeaderId, Groups, ChangeFeedOffset} Leader.shipConsumerProgress on the leader's maintenance tick Sync (server streaming) ReplicationSyncRequest{PartitionId, StartOffset, MaxBytes} → stream of ReplicationSyncResponse{Events, HasMore} Served, but no client calls it

docs.title: Leader → Follower Replication
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as Leader (partition)
    participant F as Follower
    participant INT as InternalGRPCServer :7947

    L->>L: Append to local WAL, then Replicate (publish waits)
    L->>L: Compute batch CRC32 checksum
    L->>INT: gRPC Append(ReplicationAppendRequest with term, leader ID, prev log, log start)
    INT->>F: ReplicationServiceHandler.Append
    F->>F: Accept one leader per term, verify batch CRC32
    F->>F: Check the entry at prev_log_offset, answer log_mismatch on a different term
    F->>F: Follow the leader's log start (FollowLogStart)
    F->>F: WAL.AppendReplicatedBatch, fsync in batch / every_event mode
    F-->>INT: ReplicationAppendResponse{Success, LastOffset, NextOffset, Term}
    INT-->>L: response
    L->>L: Advance follower NextOffset only on success
    L->>L: Update follower HighWatermark and ISR state
    L->>L: Acknowledge the publish once min-insync-replicas hold it

docs.title: Incremental Catch-Up (through Append)
docs.text:
When a follower is connected but reports NextOffset < events[0].Offset, Leader.catchUpFollower(f, from, to) reads [from, to) from the leader's WAL in chunks of batchSize events and at most 8 MiB, and sends each through appendToFollower, that is, the Append RPC. The Sync streaming RPC is served but no client calls it.

If the follower needs entries the leader has already removed from the start of its log, the leader first sends an Append without events that names its log start. A follower whose log ends before that start empties its log and restarts it there; the removed entries were finished before they were removed. The leader then sends from its log start. On an idle partition the leader's maintenance loop sends the same announcement (announceLogStart), so followers drop what the leader dropped without waiting for a publish.

docs.title: Bulk Snapshot Install (Snapshot)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant F as New Follower
    participant L as Leader
    participant INT as InternalGRPCServer :7947

    F->>L: gRPC Snapshot(ReplicationSnapshotRequest with the staged files it already holds)
    L->>L: Flush active segment
    loop For each segment + .index file
        L-->>F: ReplicationSnapshotChunk{Header filename, first/last_offset, file_size, crc32, is_index, reuse}
        loop 1 MB chunks, unless the file is reused
            L-->>F: ReplicationSnapshotChunk{Data}
        end
        F->>F: Verify the file's size and CRC32 against its header, fsync
    end
    L-->>F: ReplicationSnapshotChunk{Trailer success=true, last_offset, epoch}
    F->>F: Refuse a source behind the epoch this replica has accepted
    F->>F: WAL.InstallCheckpoint: journal "prepared", close segments
    F->>F: rename segments → segments.old, index → index.old
    F->>F: rename snapshot-staging/segments → segments, snapshot-staging/index → index
    F->>F: Load the new log, check that it ends at the trailer's last_offset
    F->>F: journal "installed", rm *.old, update nextOffset + epoch from trailer

Files are staged under snapshot-staging and the existing log is not touched until every file has been received and verified. A transfer that is interrupted resumes: the follower names the staged files it holds, and the leader sends only a header with reuse for those that are still current. A failure during the swap, or a crash before the journal says installed, leaves the old log in place (storage.RecoverSnapshot at the next start).

Trigger policy:

Path Trigger Code InstallSnapshot New node joins and owns partitions it does not yet have data for; a partition moves to it; a handoff target whose log differs from the stopped leader's PartitionManager.SyncPartitionFromLeader (10-minute context), called from internal/cluster/manager.go, router.go and leadership.go catchUpFollower over Append Connected follower reports lag during normal Replicate Leader.catchUpFollower Automatic lag-driven InstallSnapshot Not implemented. No mid-flight lag monitor calls InstallSnapshot; --snapshot-catchup-threshold is not read. See Known Limitations

docs.title: Replication mTLS
docs.text:
With --replication-tls-enabled, all traffic between nodes runs over CA-pinned mutual TLS, independent of public-API TLS: replication gRPC, membership and Raft (internal/replication/mtls.go, internal/cluster/transport.go). The configuration is read into replication.MTLSConfig{Enabled, CAFile, CertFile, KeyFile, ServerName} and consumed by replication.BuildClientTLS (callers) and replication.BuildServerTLSConfig (servers, tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert).

Certificates, keys and the CA are read again when their files change, without a restart (internal/tlsfiles): the TLS configuration uses GetCertificate / GetClientCertificate, and the files are checked at most every 2 seconds when a handshake needs them. The public gRPC port and the HTTP port reload their certificates the same way.

Without the flag, nodes use insecure credentials. That is allowed only with --dev; production mode refuses it in config.ValidateConfig.

docs.title: Reliability notes
docs.text:
• Append path: per-batch CRC32 verified before WAL.AppendReplicatedBatch; term fencing rejects stale-leader replays; leader advances NextOffset only on success.
  • Snapshot path: every file's size and CRC32 verified; the directory swap is journaled (WAL.InstallCheckpoint), which loads the segment list and sparse index from the new files and keeps the old ones until the new log has been checked.
  • Quorum: Leader.Replicate returns success only after min-insync-replicas replicas including the leader have appended. Default is 1 (leader-only); production target is RF=3 / minISR=2 (see Consistency and Guarantees).
  • Durability on followers: in batch and every_event fsync modes a follower syncs a replicated batch before it answers Append.
  • Trigger gap: --snapshot-catchup-threshold is a dead config key — parsed but never read; SyncPartitionFromLeader installs a snapshot unconditionally when it is called. There is still no mid-flight lag watcher that automatically switches a connected follower from incremental catch-up to InstallSnapshot. See Known Limitations.

docs.title: Replay Engine
docs.text: The replay engine allows consumers to re-read historical events by time range or offset.

docs.title: Replay Modes
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Replay Request] --> B{Mode?}

    B -->|start_ts + end_ts| C[Time-Range Replay]
    C --> C1[Chunked cursor over offsets 0 to last, with a schedule_ts filter]
    C1 --> C2[Skip segments whose time span misses the window - WAL.TimeSpan]
    C2 --> C3[Stream to client via gRPC]

    B -->|start_offset + count| D[Offset-Based Replay]
    D --> D1[Chunked cursor over start_offset to start_offset + count - 1]

docs.title: Prometheus Metrics
docs.text:
Category Key Metrics API cronos_api_grpc_requests_total{method, status}, cronos_api_grpc_request_duration_seconds{method} WAL cronos_wal_append_latency_seconds{partition}, cronos_wal_segment_count{partition}, cronos_wal_high_watermark{partition} Scheduler cronos_scheduler_ready_events{partition}, cronos_scheduler_active_timers{partition}, cronos_timing_wheel_overflow_level{partition}, cronos_scheduler_cold_store_entries{partition}, cronos_scheduler_hydrated_events_total{partition}, cronos_scheduler_hydrator_interval_ms{partition}, cronos_scheduler_hydrator_scan_duration_seconds{partition} Dedup cronos_dedup_check_latency_seconds{partition, path}, cronos_dedup_bloom_memory_bytes{partition}, cronos_dedup_bloom_false_positive_rate{partition} Delivery cronos_dispatch_latency_seconds{partition}, cronos_consumer_group_lag{group, partition}, cronos_delivery_lateness_seconds{partition} (time between an event's scheduled time and its first delivery) Accounting cronos_events_accepted_total{partition}, cronos_events_duplicate_total{partition}, cronos_events_delivered_total{partition, attempt} (first or retry), cronos_events_acknowledged_total{partition, result}, cronos_events_delivery_timeouts_total{partition}, cronos_events_dead_lettered_total{partition} Memory cronos_memory_held_bytes (what the process holds and cannot hand back), cronos_memory_limit_bytes (what it may use). Publishes are refused at --max-memory-percent of the limit Log cronos_wal_log_start_offset{partition}, cronos_wal_segments_removed_total{partition}, cronos_change_feed_offset{partition} Admission cronos_admission_rejected_total{partition} Cluster cronos_cluster_nodes_alive, cronos_cluster_partitions_leader, cronos_replication_lag{partition, follower} (in events), cronos_clock_skew_ms{source_node, target_node}

The accounting counters follow an event from the acknowledged publish to the acknowledged delivery, on the partition's leader. Rates that do not add up show where events are: accepted faster than delivered means events are waiting for their time or for a consumer; delivered faster than acknowledged, with timeouts, means consumers are not keeping up; attempt="retry" and dead letters mean deliveries are failing. The counters start at zero when a node starts and move with leadership, so compare rates summed over the nodes, not totals. cronos_wal_high_watermark - cronos_wal_log_start_offset is how many events a partition's log holds; cronos_wal_high_watermark - cronos_change_feed_offset is the change feed's lag.

• W3C TraceContext propagation

docs.title: Startup and Bootstrap Sequence
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[main.go starts] --> B[Load config from flags + CRONOS_* env<br/>production validation unless --dev]
    B --> B1[Memory limit, audit, schema, tenant, CDC, SLO, tracing]
    B1 --> C[Create shared PebbleDB cache 256MB and the partition manager]
    C --> C1[Start disk monitor, backup scheduler, retention loop]
    C1 --> D{Cluster enabled?}

    D -->|Yes| E[Create Raft node]
    E --> F{Raft state on disk?}
    F -->|Yes| H[Stay in the cluster the state names]
    F -->|No| F1{No other seed, or --cluster-bootstrap and<br/>every other seed says it has no cluster?}
    F1 -->|Yes| G[Bootstrap Raft as a single-node cluster]
    F1 -->|No| H1[Create nothing, join through the seeds]
    G --> I[Start membership and the router with its hash ring]
    H --> I
    H1 --> I
    I --> K[Create partition 0 only - others are created when first used]

    D -->|No| L[Create all partitions locally]

    K --> M[Start partitions]
    L --> M
    M --> N[Per partition: open WAL + schedule the events not yet due + init cold store<br/>+ start scheduler, hydrator, worker, delivery, compaction and change feed]
    N --> O[Create public gRPC server with interceptors]
    O --> P[Register Event, ConsumerGroup, Partition and Admin services<br/>Transaction only with --experimental-features]
    P --> P1[Internal gRPC: Replication, Raft in cluster mode<br/>CrossRegion only with --experimental-features]
    P1 --> Q[Start gRPC on :9000 and :7947]
    Q --> R[Start HTTP on :8080: health, metrics, dashboard, admin API]
    R --> S[Wait for SIGINT or SIGTERM]

A node with --cluster-bootstrap asks every other node in --cluster-seeds whether it belongs to a cluster, and waits for as long as one of them does not answer (internal/cluster/bootstrap.go). One node that has Raft state is enough for it not to create a cluster: a node that comes back with an empty disk joins the cluster it belonged to instead of starting a second one.

docs.title: Graceful Shutdown Sequence
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[SIGINT or SIGTERM received] --> B[Cancel context, 60s for everything below]
    B --> C[Public and internal gRPC GracefulStopWithTimeout, 25s]
    C --> D{Graceful drain within timeout?}
    D -->|Yes| E[HTTP server Shutdown, 5s]
    D -->|No| F[Forced gRPC Stop]
    F --> E
    E --> G[Stop retention loop and backup scheduler]
    G --> H[PartitionManager.Close: StopAllPartitions]
    H --> I[Per partition: stop delivery loops + stop scheduler and worker<br/>+ drain dispatcher up to 30s + close DLQ, stores and WAL]
    I --> J[Stop cluster manager: Raft shutdown, then membership]
    J --> K[Final WAL flush]
    K --> L[Exit]

Start() exposes ServeError() so callers can observe unexpected gRPC server exits, and health-server startup errors are propagated.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: The historical claim of 1,010,933 events/s across 96 million events has no preserved benchmark artifact or durability verification. The current three-node validation reports the exact workloads, accepted-event rates, baseline comparison, and remaining correctness limits. All three nodes ran on one physical machine.

docs.title: Optimization Techniques

The full list of flags, with defaults and the production checks, is in docs/architecture/features/config.md and in cronos-api --help. It is kept there only, so that it is not kept twice. The flags that shape a deployment:

Category Flag Default Description Node --node-id required Unique node identifier Node --data-dir ./data Data directory Node --partition-count 1 Number of partitions Node --dev false Disable the production requirements, for local development Ports --grpc-addr :9000 Public gRPC Ports --http-addr :8080 Health, metrics, dashboard and admin API; over TLS with --http-tls-enabled Ports --cluster-gossip-addr, --cluster-grpc-addr, --cluster-raft-addr :7946, :7947, :7948 Membership, replication and Raft between nodes WAL --segment-size 512MB Segment size before rotation WAL --fsync-mode batch every_event, batch, or periodic (--dev only) Scheduler --hot-window-minutes 60 Events due later than this are kept on disk as references (0 = disabled) Delivery --ack-timeout 30s How long a delivery may stay unacknowledged before it is retried Delivery --max-retries 5 Retries before an event goes to the dead-letter queue Memory --max-memory-percent 80 Publishes are refused while the process holds this share of its memory limit Memory --memory-limit 0 Memory limit in bytes (0 = the container's limit, or the machine's memory) Retention --retention-max-age-hours 168 Segments older than this are removed (0 = disabled) Retention --compaction-interval 10m How often a partition removes segments whose events are all finished Backup --backup-interval, --backup-retention, --backup-dir 1h, 168h, backups under the data directory When backups are taken, how long they are kept, and where Replication --replication-factor 1 Replicas per partition (production requires 3 or more) Replication --min-insync-replicas 1 Replicas, the leader included, that must hold a write before it is acknowledged (production requires 2 or more) Replication --replication-tls-enabled false Mutual TLS for replication, membership and Raft Cluster --cluster false Enable cluster mode Cluster --cluster-seeds empty Membership addresses of the cluster's nodes; Environment variables: every flag also reads CRONOS_<FLAG>, the flag's name in upper case with dashes as underscores (--fsync-mode is CRONOS_FSYNC_MODE).
